title: Too Time-Crunched to Seek Variety: The Influence of Parenting Motivation on Consumer Variety Seeking
eligible_reason: Study 1 is a staggered binary-treatment design (households become parents at different dates, later parents act as controls, 2004-2015 NielsenIQ panel, SEs clustered by household), so the design qualifies. Every main-text specification (Table 3, Columns 1-4) includes time-varying household demographics and extra fixed effects (category quantity, basket quantity, day of week, day of month), so none qualifies under PROTOCOL Section 2. Studies 2-5 are randomized experiments.
design_notes: Equation: vari_Ct = delta*1(Parent)_it + CatWeek_iCt + DayofWeek_it + DayofMonth_it + CatQuant_iCt + TripQuant_it + Demo_it + alpha_iC + eps. The sample contains only ever-treated households, so identification is from not-yet-treated households (average 897 control households per focal household). Pre-trend check with 1, 2, 3 year lead dummies is in Web Appendix Table W3 (not main text, also includes controls). Robustness in Web Appendix Tables W4-W5. Whether a no-controls version could be estimated depends on obtaining the NielsenIQ extract and authors' code; none is listed.
estimators_reported: TWFE-style DiD with household-category and category-week FE plus controls (Table 3)
main_or_robustness: main (Study 1 of six studies; the experiments carry the mechanism)
screener_notes: No replication package or regressions file was listed in the batch file (package_dir and regressions_path empty); screening is from the article text only. Study 1 uses licensed NielsenIQ Consumer Panel data via the Kilts Center (acknowledgment near the end of the paper), which authors cannot redistribute. Number of adoption cohorts is not stated; parental-status change is observed at the annual demographic file level, so cohorts are by first parental year (2004-2015 window). Set eligible_design=false because no main-text specification is eligible; staggered_design_present=true records that the design itself is staggered. A reviewer may want to request a no-controls version from the authors, but it is not in the article.

No version without these controls appears in the main text.

ineligible_specs.unit: household x shopping trip x category
ineligible_specs.time_unit: calendar week (category-specific week FE); parental status switches at household-specific date
ineligible_specs.fe: household-category, category-week, category quantity, basket (trip) quantity, day of week, day of month
ineligible_specs.sample: NielsenIQ households with no children at the start of data and children during 2004-2015 (2,049 households, 887,648 trips, 1,511,092 household-trip-category observations in col 1); all households eventually treated, later parents serve as controls for earlier parents; cols 2-4 restrict to category purchase quantity > 1, 2, 3
